transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, good to meet you too. Um… I guess the main thing is I’ve been getting pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and then one Slack ping, or even a song lyric, or just some random idea for another project, and suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread. It’s not like I’m trying to avoid it, I just… get derailed, if that makes sense.
Did you have this same kind of getting easily distracted when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I was a pretty good kid overall, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but even in elementary school my teachers would write things like that I rushed through worksheets or didn’t fully keep track of the directions.

And I guess during group work I’d sometimes talk over other kids without really meaning to. At home, my parents would sit next to me while I did homework because otherwise I’d kind of wander off or start doing something else before I finished. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are these concentration problems causing significant trouble for you at work?

Yeah… I mean, I’m not in a regular job right now, so I don’t want to overstate it. But with freelance stuff and projects, it has caused problems.

I’ve lost a couple of small contracts because I didn’t follow through as cleanly as people expected, or I’d miss pieces and then it made me look unreliable. And there was a portfolio competition I wanted to do, and I basically missed out because I couldn’t get everything together properly.

It’s embarrassing, because I do care and I think my ideas are good… but some friends or collaborators seem hesitant to work with me now. Not because they dislike me, I don’t think, just because they’re not sure they can count on me to finish things smoothly. Does that answer what you mean by “significant trouble”?
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a constant way, at least. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, like whether I’m doing things right or if I’ve disappointed someone, but I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about lots of different things when nothing’s actually happening.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean? I wouldn’t want to say no if I’m just not recognizing it.
Have you felt down or depressed most days for a long time?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of low or frustrated with myself, but not like… depressed most days for a long time. At least I wouldn’t describe it that way.

Does that make sense?
Did these concentration problems start after a particularly stressful event in your life?

I don’t think it started after one big stressful event, no.

It’s kind of embarrassing to say, but it goes pretty far back. Even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I rushed through worksheets, or I lost track of directions, or talked over other kids during group work. My parents used to have to sit next to me while I did homework because otherwise I’d wander off or start doing something else before I finished.

So… I don’t think it was caused by a specific stressful thing. It’s more like it’s always kind of been there, if that makes sense.
